title: Hate Personified: Investigating the role of LLMs in content moderation
findings: LLMs' hate speech annotations vary significantly when primed with different religious personas. The models are sensitive to these contextual cues, and their perception of hatefulness changes based on the religious identity they are asked to assume. The study also found that explicitly known religious-based vulnerabilities, such as Islamophobia in the context of Arabic posts annotated by a 'Muslim' persona, are better captured by the LLM, leading to higher sensitivity in detecting related hate speech.

measurement_description: The study measured how priming Large Language Models (LLMs) with different religious personas (e.g., Christian, Muslim, Jewish, etc.) affects their hate speech annotations. It evaluated the change in inter-annotator agreement (IAA) and the predicted hate label ratio (PHLR) to understand the model's sensitivity to religious identity traits.
